instruction:
Use the ANSYS Workbench GUI to complete a nonlinear Static Structural contact analysis.

Physical problem:
An elastic steel sphere presses against an elastic steel plate through frictionless contact.

Coordinate system and geometry:
- Use the global Cartesian coordinate system.
- Use a full 3D model.
- The vertical loading direction is the negative global Y direction.
- The plate is centered about the global origin in the X-Z plane.
- The plate dimensions are:
  - X direction: 100 mm
  - Z direction: 100 mm
  - Y direction thickness: 10 mm
- Place the plate so that:
  - The top surface is at Y = 0 mm
  - The bottom surface is at Y = -10 mm
- The sphere radius is 10 mm.
- Place the sphere above the plate with its center on the global Y axis.
- The lower point of the sphere should initially contact the center of the plate top surface.

Model parameters:
- Sphere material: Structural Steel
- Plate material: Structural Steel
- Use the following linear elastic properties for both bodies:
  - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa
  - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3
- Mesh:
  - Use local refinement in the contact region.
  - Local element size in the contact region: 0.3 mm
  - Element size away from the contact region: 2 mm

Contact setup:
- Contact pair: sphere surface against the top surface of the plate.
- Contact type: Frictionless.
- Contact formulation: Augmented Lagrange or Pure Penalty.
- Use appropriate normal contact stiffness settings to obtain a converged nonlinear contact solution.

Boundary conditions and load:
- Fix the bottom face of the plate.
- Apply a vertical compressive force of 500 N to the sphere in the negative global Y direction.
- Prevent only the unnecessary rigid-body lateral motion of the sphere, while allowing the sphere to move vertically into contact with the plate.
- Do not fully fix the sphere.

Analysis type:
- Nonlinear Static Structural analysis.
- Enable large deflection.
- Use automatic time stepping or sufficient load substeps to obtain a converged contact solution.

Save requirements:
- Use C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop as the working location.
- Save the Workbench project file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_hertz.wbpj
- Save the MAPDL-equivalent database file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_hertz.db
- Save the MAPDL-equivalent structural result file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_hertz.rst
